name: Hugging Face / Transformers
bestFor: Reference execution, model research, and embedded Python integration.
benefit: Use transparent reference execution to calibrate routing, positions, model topology, and memory-use behavior before moving to a serving engine.
why: Hugging Face gives model developers the clearest view of attention semantics and the broadest surface for controlled compatibility work.

tested.topology: Model-family adapters preserve native cache and local/global attention organization

recommendation.useWhen: You need semantic correctness, model calibration, or direct Python integration.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You need production continuous batching or fleet-level serving.
recommendation.gate: Broader workload qualification remains model and domain dependent.

limitations: Routing quality is model- and domain-dependent.
Frozen sparse memory has a depth-dependent compatibility band.
Serving throughput and tail latency are not the focus of the reference runtime.

name: vLLM
bestFor: High-throughput open-model serving on NVIDIA infrastructure.
benefit: Keep exact prefix reuse separate from query-addressed PRA resources, then test whether shared immutable memory reduces repeated prefill and HBM pressure.
why: vLLM is a common production serving choice for open models, where selected context can be evaluated before deeper scheduler integration.

tested.topology: Native path requires geometry-matched selected K/V and request-local lifetime

recommendation.useWhen: You want a low-risk evaluation with an existing OpenAI-compatible serving stack.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You require a production-qualified E2 or E3 lifecycle today.
recommendation.gate: Import matched quality-adjusted serving results and tested versions into the product registry.

limitations: Native E2 is not promoted as production validated.
LMCache/WARM economics are not measured in the website export.
Scheduler-owned E3 remains in progress.

name: SGLang
bestFor: Advanced serving, RadixAttention, and hierarchical cache research.
benefit: Compose exact radix-prefix reuse with semantic-resource identity, asynchronous movement, and reactivation of archived non-prefix memory.
why: SGLang exposes sophisticated cache and scheduler mechanisms that make the boundary between prefix identity and semantic identity especially useful to test.

tested.topology: Radix prefix state and PRA resources retain distinct identities

recommendation.useWhen: You use SGLang and want to measure selected context without changing scheduler semantics.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You depend on qualified off-node HiCache PRA behavior.
recommendation.gate: Matched E0/E2/E3 serving economics and tested configurations.

limitations: Off-node HiCache behavior is not measured in the website export.
Native resource reuse is experimental.
Scheduler integration remains a research path.

name: MLX / MLX-LM
bestFor: Local AI and unified-memory inference on Apple Silicon.
benefit: Treat the semantic archive separately from rotating sequential KV and evaluate quality, unified-memory use, and latency together.
why: MLX is a strong local inference environment where model state and caches share unified memory and memory tradeoffs are directly visible.

tested.topology: Rotating/local KV and persistent semantic memory are evaluated separately

recommendation.useWhen: You want a local Apple Silicon baseline and can measure unified-memory pressure.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You require a production-qualified fused E2 implementation.
recommendation.gate: Live fused E2 measurements and tested version export.

limitations: Live fused E2 is not presented as validated.
Model/version combinations are not yet exported.
Quality-memory-latency results remain incomplete.

name: OpenVINO GenAI / OVMS
bestFor: Intel CPU, GPU, NPU, Windows, edge, and enterprise deployments.
benefit: Reduce selected sequential context first, then evaluate whether a native non-prefix memory seam improves device-memory and batching behavior.
why: OpenVINO reaches hardware and operating environments that differ from CUDA-first serving, including Intel edge and AI-PC deployments.

tested.topology: Native selected-KV seam remains under qualification

recommendation.useWhen: You can participate in controlled Intel hardware evaluation.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You need a validated deployment profile now.
recommendation.gate: Establish a reproducible E0 baseline before native E2 promotion.

limitations: E0 results are not yet imported into the site registry.
Native E2 is not validated.
Device-specific measurements are pending.

name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
bestFor: NVIDIA-centric deployments focused on optimized production inference.
benefit: Evaluate semantic selected context alongside paged KV, prefix reuse, in-flight batching, connectors, and disaggregated serving without conflating resource and prefix identity.
why: TensorRT-LLM is a natural target for teams optimizing latency and throughput on NVIDIA fleets.

tested.topology: Paged selected blocks must be request-local and isolated from prefix state

recommendation.useWhen: You can benchmark against a geometry-matched E0 baseline.
recommendation.avoidWhen: You need a validated native connector profile today.
recommendation.gate: Reproducible E0/E2 serving economics and connector lifecycle tests.

limitations: Tables in the current research draft contain unfilled metrics.
Native attachment and connector persistence are not validated for launch.
No tested version matrix is exported.

name: AirLLM
bestFor: Feasibility experiments where model weights exceed accelerator memory.
benefit: Virtualize model weights and semantic context independently, while measuring disk and PCIe contention instead of assuming both streaming systems compose for free.
why: AirLLM explores a distinct low-VRAM regime where weight streaming and context streaming compete for bandwidth.

tested.topology: Layer-streamed weights and layer-local PRA K/V require coordinated scheduling

recommendation.useWhen: Your primary constraint is model-weight fit and you can instrument I/O contention.
recommendation.gate: Complete the E0/E2 memory and I/O frontier with tested configurations.

limitations: Current research tables contain unfilled metrics.
E2 remains research-only.
Disk/PCIe contention has not been qualified for production.
